title: What the core-v1 engine can do
text: The engine plays only the Command Phase: on a turn a side activates a system with a leader from its pool, moves its own units into it, finishes the activation, or passes. Combat, missions, production, deployment, recruiting, probe droids, objectives, loyalty and subjugation are not implemented: rules about them do not apply, and only the actions listed by the engine exist.

title: core-v1 has no combat
text: The core-v1 engine never resolves combat: units of both sides may stand in one system, which the UI marks as contested. Tactic cards, dice, damage, retreat and battle wins do not exist yet.

title: core-v1 has no missions and an empty Assignment Phase
text: There are no mission cards in core-v1: the Assignment Phase passes automatically and a Command Phase turn can only activate a system or pass. Mission-driven effects (loyalty, capture, new base, Death Star projects) are missing.

title: core-v1 Refresh: only retrieve leaders and advance time
text: The core-v1 Refresh Phase runs only step 1 (all leaders return) and the time advance of step 5. Drawing missions, probe droids, objectives, recruiting, building and deploying are not implemented.

title: core-v1 has no objectives: reputation never moves
text: Without objective cards the reputation marker stays on 14, so the Rebels can only win by surviving until the time marker reaches 14.

title: core-v1 does not model loyalty or subjugation
text: core-v1 has no loyalty or subjugation markers: activation step 5 (subjugate) is skipped, the first game loyalty markers are not placed, and Imperial loyalty cannot reveal the base.

title: core-v1 has no voluntary base reveal
text: The Rebel side cannot reveal its base voluntarily in core-v1; the base is only revealed by Imperial ground units.

title: core-v1 chooses the base system itself
text: The engine picks the base deterministically from the game id among eligible systems instead of letting the Rebel player choose. Besides the official first game limits it also excludes systems holding starting Rebel units (Bothawui), so that the hidden base is not given away on the first screen.

title: core-v1 merges the Rebel Base space with the base system
text: In core-v1 units "on the Rebel Base space" simply stand in the base's system (hidden from the Empire). There is no separate space: no activation of the space, no movement from it to systems adjacent to the base, and a leader in the base system locks all units there.

title: core-v1 reveals the base by a central state check
text: After every accepted command and at game creation core-v1 reveals the base once if an Imperial ground unit stands in its system; during an Imperial activation the reveal waits until the activation's movement ends (FINISH_ACTIVATION). Imperial loyalty does not exist, so it cannot reveal the base.

title: core-v1 always uses the first game setup
text: Every core-v1 game starts from the fixed first game unit placement; the standard (advanced) setup with random loyalty and free placement is not available, and no decks or action cards are prepared.

title: core-v1 has only the starting leaders
text: Only the four starting leaders of each side exist in core-v1; recruitable leaders, action cards and the Super Star Destroyer (which reaches the build queue only through a card ability) never enter play.

title: core-v1 rejects PASS during an own activation
text: core-v1 answers PASS during the actor's running activation with activationInProgress: the activation has to be finished first.

title: core-v1 checks transport per MOVE_PIECES command
text: A MOVE_PIECES command moves units from one source system, and transport capacity is counted only among the ships moving in that same command. Units needing transport must therefore move in the same command as their carriers; a ship moved in an earlier command gives no capacity.

title: core-v1 does not enforce component limits
text: Nothing in core-v1 creates new units, leaders or markers, so component limits are never reached and are not modelled.
